articles.title: Star-B-Que Report
articles.summary: The 1999 FPOA/AANC Star-B-Que, held on July 10th to avoid a total solar eclipse, was a successful astronomy social event. It welcomed new Fremont Peak State Park ranger Cameron Bowers and gathered members from numerous astronomy clubs across California. The festivities included a BBQ, potluck dishes, and an "Astronomical Gastronomical" dessert contest featuring creatively themed entries.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document presents the August and September 1999 activities calendar for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It details various events including multiple star parties at locations like Houge Park, Fremont Peak, and Pinnacles Nat'l Monument, alongside observational astronomy classes and general meetings featuring topics such as eyepiece projection and equipment nights. Practical information like sunset and moon phase times is also provided for observing events.

articles.title: Star-B-Que Report, 1999
articles.summary: The 1999 Star-B-Que event was a vibrant gathering featuring astronomy-themed contests, including an intricate Apollo 11 cake and creative asterism designs. Awards were presented to amateur, commercial, and professional contributors, and a raffle distributed numerous prizes. The evening culminated in a twilight talk on the moon by Bob Garfinkle, followed by extensive and successful stargazing with many telescopes despite initial cloudy conditions.

articles.title: General Meeting June 26, 1999
articles.summary: This article details a General Meeting held on June 26, 1999, which included an all-night observing session at Fremont Peak Observatory where guests viewed numerous celestial objects through various telescopes, culminating in observations of Jupiter and Saturn. The meeting also featured a talk by 'Bob' on lunar rays and bright spots, delving into their characteristics, historical theories, and modern scientific understanding based on spacecraft and Apollo missions, concluding with observing tips.

articles.title: Mark Taylor
articles.summary: Mark Taylor describes volunteering to set up his 8" LX-200 telescope for 58 kindergartners during their school sleepover. Despite challenging viewing conditions, the children were thrilled to observe the Moon, Venus, and Mars, demonstrating their capacity to appreciate celestial objects and engage with astronomy. The event was a significant success, fostering excitement and appreciation among the young students and teachers alike.

articles.title: Dave North
articles.summary: This article from August 1999 highlights two key astronomical events: a solar eclipse on August 11 and a western libration with a full moon on August 26. The author encourages readers to observe the latter event, focusing on the rare opportunity to view the Orientale Basin and its unique features like the "Weird Big Mountain," emphasizing its scientific importance despite potential viewing challenges. While he won't attend the eclipse, he anticipates reports from other members.

articles.title: Showtime For Meteors, Part I
articles.summary: This article, "Showtime For Meteors, Part I," details two significant meteor showers: the Perseids and the Alpha Aurigids. It highlights the Perseids as the year's most popular shower, occurring August 11-13, and discusses a new peak activity observed since 1991, with predictions for 1999's rates and viewing conditions. The article also covers the Alpha Aurigids, known for a brief but sharp peak around August 31/September 1, noting potential visibility for observers in dark skies despite moonlight in 1999.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article, "The Shallow Sky," details planetary observing opportunities for August. It notes Mars is dim but still visible, while Uranus and Neptune are close in Capricornus and good targets for binoculars and small telescopes. Pluto is also well-placed in Ophiuchus for experienced observers. Early morning risers can enjoy Jupiter and Saturn, with Mercury and Venus appearing later in the month.

articles.title: About SJAA Star Parties
articles.summary: This article outlines three primary star party locations organized by the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association), each offering different observing experiences. Houge Park is recommended for beginners and offers both lunar and deep-sky views, while Henry Coe State Park and Fremont Peak State Park provide increasingly darker skies for serious amateur astronomers. Directions to these sites can be obtained via a dedicated hotline.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: This article provides updates on several active comets, including Comet Lee, Comet LINEAR (1998 T1), and Periodic Comet Tempel 2, noting their current visibility. It also reports on recent comet discoveries by the SOHO satellite, the LINEAR program, and the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. The author includes notes on amateur comet hunting, analyzing the perihelion distances of amateur-discovered comets and contrasting them with those found by satellite programs.

articles.title: Ephemerides
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for two comets, C/1999 H1 (Lee) and C/1998 T1 (LINEAR). For each comet, tables list date-specific celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elevation, and estimated visual magnitudes, serving as a guide for observers to locate and track them from July through early September.

articles.title: Periodic Comet Tempel 2 (P/55)
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for Periodic Comet Tempel 2 (P/55), detailing its celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), elongation, and estimated visual magnitude. The data spans from early July to early September, allowing observers to track the comet's position and brightness over time. It serves as a guide for locating the comet in the night sky.

articles.title: Elements
articles.summary: This document presents detailed orbital elements for three celestial objects: "Lee", "LINEAR (T1)", and "P/Tempel 2". For each object, key astronomical data such as perihelion date and distance, eccentricity, inclination, and orbital period are listed, along with their respective references. Contact information for Don Machholz is also provided.

articles.title: August 1999
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical ephemeris for August 1999, primarily for observers in the Pacific Daylight Time zone. It details lunar phases, daily rise, transit, and set times for the Moon and several planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn), along with their magnitudes, distances (A.U.), right ascension, and declination. Additionally, it includes information on solar data, astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and specifies the darkest Saturday night for observation.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and board of directors for an organization, including their titles such as President, VP, Secretary, Treasurer, and Director. Each individual's name and a contact phone number are provided for reference.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: The document lists the staff involved with "Ephemeris", including two editors, two individuals responsible for circulation, and the printing company. Each staff member and the company are provided with a contact phone number.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris, the official newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly throughout the year, from January to December. The statement also provides the mailing address for the San Jose Astronomical Association in Campbell, CA.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides loaner telescopes to its members. All available scopes can be borrowed by any SJAA member. Members interested in borrowing should contact Mike Koop via email or phone to make arrangements.

articles.title: Stored Scopes
articles.summary: The article lists various telescopes, referred to as 'Stored Scopes,' that are available for immediate loan to members of SJAA. These scopes are currently stored at the homes of other SJAA members. Interested members should contact Mike Koop to arrange a pickup at any SJAA event.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes currently on loan, detailing each scope's description, the borrower, and the due date. It also informs interested members that they can be placed on a waiting list for a scope to become available after its due date.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes with extended loan periods available for borrowing. Interested individuals can request to borrow one, and the organization will coordinate a transfer time with the current borrower. The list includes details such as scope type, current borrower, and due date (if specified).

articles.title: Waiting List:
articles.summary: The document presents a 'Waiting List' which, at the moment, is entirely empty. It features columns for 'Scope Description' and 'Borrower', suggesting it is intended to track items or individuals awaiting something, but currently there are no entries.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: This document, from the August 1999 SJAA Ephemeris, encourages members to submit articles for publication in the Ephemeris, providing an email address for submissions. It also provides instructions for subscribing to or unsubscribing from the SJAA Mailing List.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for new or renewal memberships, including standard and junior rates, and an optional subscription to Sky and Telescope magazine. It provides instructions for submission, requiring checks payable to SJAA, and can be brought to a meeting or mailed to their P.O. Box in Campbell, CA, along with contact information.
